# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 65 (Bu-Vb Pc65)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc65
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 65
**Title (English, from literature):** Ordaining a person under twenty
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Unlike the corresponding regulations for female candidates, which distinguish between married girls and unmarried maidens (*kumāribhūtā*), the rule for men stipulates a single uniform minimum age of twenty [Hüsken 1997].

Full canonical parallels exist across the Vinaya traditions of other early Buddhist schools, including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya, preserved in Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit recensions, as well as a Gāndhārī Prātimokṣa fragment. In the Pali canon, the rule shares substantial phraseology and passage-level parallels with the ordination procedures of the *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (specifically Pācittiya 65 and 71), and several Nikāya discourses (including MN 2, MN 125, and AN 4.165) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects textual reuse with Sanskrit monastic corpora (including the *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya*) and Tibetan translations of the *Vinayavibhaṅga* and *Vinayavastu* [DharmaNexus].
